## Overview

Internal prefill checkpoints (#52789, generalized in #57783; Mamba2 in #57329) export a prefill's block-boundary state from inside one forward, so in `mamba_cache_mode="align"` the scheduler no longer stops the prefill at its last block boundary. #60050 does this for the FlashInfer GDN prefill backend. This PR extends the same shared checkpoint mechanism to the **Triton/FLA** (CUDA, ROCm) and **AITER FlyDSL** (ROCm) GDN prefill backends, whose chunk kernels return only each sequence's final state. No kernel changes.

## Claims

- Qwen3.5-27B on 8x MI308X (TP8, AITER FlyDSL prefill), 8000-token prompts, post-rebase A/B: mean TTFT −11.4% at concurrency 4 and −18.6% at 16. This is consistent with the two pre-rebase runs (−11% to −12% and −16% to −17%). Throughput is unchanged and TPOT is +3%. At concurrency 1, TTFT is +11.8% on this setup; see Details.
- GSM8K is within run-to-run variation: original A/B 0.9636 baseline vs 0.9651 with this PR; post-rebase on the same nightly, main 0.9636 vs this PR 0.9606 (`d907ca3d8`) and 0.9636 (current head).
- Outputs, final states and exported checkpoints match the unsplit computation (both backends, fp32 and bf16 state). On the Qwen3.5-27B server, after the same primer prompt on both servers, resuming from a checkpoint this PR exported gives the same greedy tokens and logprobs, bit for bit, as resuming from the state main stores at that boundary.
- Batches without a checkpoint are unchanged. This is not enabled with speculative decoding or `prefix_match_unit` smaller than the block size.

## Validation

**Post-rebase TTFT A/B**: 8x MI308X, Qwen3.5-27B BF16, TP8, rebased head `d907ca3d8`, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-3f1bcfd82`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `gdn_prefill_backend=aiter_flydsl`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`. Both arms add `--block-size 64`, which gives a 448-token block: an 8000-token prompt's last boundary is then at 7616 with a 384-token tail. `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 8000 in / 1000 out, `--ignore-eos`, 16 prompts per unit of concurrency, a fresh server per arm, and 0% prefix-cache hits. Both servers reported zero errors.

| Concurrency | TTFT mean, baseline → this PR | TTFT mean Δ | TTFT p50 Δ | TTFT p99 Δ | TPOT Δ | Output tok/s Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 518.2 → 579.4 ms | +11.8% | +11.7% | +11.9% | 0.0% | −0.9% |
| 4 | 1555.2 → 1377.3 ms | −11.4% | −23.9% | +4.4% | +3.1% | −1.0% |
| 16 | 3112.6 → 2534.2 ms | −18.6% | −17.5% | −7.0% | +3.2% | +0.1% |

The current head only changes how the builder opts in and adds an assertion, so this A/B was not repeated.

**GSM8K**: evalscope, 1319 questions, 4-shot, thinking off, greedy. The original same-server A/B was 0.9636 baseline vs 0.9651 with this PR. After rebasing onto #60050 and current main, a matched A/B on nightly `3f1bcfd82` was 0.9636 baseline vs 0.9606 with this PR (4 fewer questions); this is within the variation seen across repeated runs with lossy INT4 all-reduce and dynamic batching. The 4-shot prompts (~690 tokens) cross the 448-token block, and the post-rebase PR run reached a 65% prefix-cache hit rate, so it exercised exported checkpoints. There were no server errors. The current head scored 0.9636 on the same setup.

**Resuming from an exported checkpoint** (same server setup, greedy, 32 output tokens with logprobs; random-token and English prompts of 3000 and 8000 tokens, two seeds): a primer one token past the last block boundary (2689 / 7617 tokens) caches the state at 2688 / 7616, which this PR exports from a split row and main stores at the end of a chunk. Resuming the full prompt from it gives identical tokens and logprobs on the two servers in all 8 cases. Cold runs are not bitwise equal between the two, since this PR runs each prompt in one step where main runs two; for the same reason this PR's cold and resumed runs are not bitwise equal, while main's are.

**New test** `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_prefill_checkpoint.py`: real `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` and `_forward_core`, with the KV cache spec from `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention.get_kv_cache_spec`, `{triton, aiter_flydsl} x {fp32, bf16 state} x {0, 1 decode rows}`, on a batch with two checkpointed prefills (with and without an initial state) and one without. Checkpoint slots are compared with a forward that stops at each checkpoint (conv window exact, recurrent state within tolerance); outputs and final states with the same batch without checkpoints. The forward must fail when a checkpoint is scheduled without the split. A second test checks that the builder enables the split for a Qwen GDN layer whether the spec's alignment is 1 or the block size, and not for another layer on the GDN backend. All 10 cases pass.

**Post-rebase validation**: rebased onto current main `8f111b22e` after #60050, #60645 and #61569; tested on 8x MI308X with `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-3f1bcfd82`.

- New test plus related GDN/checkpoint tests (current head): 110 passed, 28 skipped.
- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py`: 39 passed with AITER disabled. With AITER enabled, one mixed-prefill/spec-decode comparison fails identically on the unmodified nightly because #60645 makes the shared GDN reference select FlyDSL while Kimi KDA does not; this is not caused by this PR.
- No host/device sync in the split chunk call or checkpoint export on either backend (sync debug guard also catches a control `Tensor.item()`).
- `pre-commit run` over the PR's changes passes, including mypy and test tethering.
- End-to-end Qwen3.5-27B server: block size 448, AITER FlyDSL prefill active, checkpoint-reserved KV capacity, smoke request and GSM8K successful, no server errors.

## Details

- **Split**: the builder cuts each checkpointed row at its checkpoint in the prefill varlen batch; only a row's first segment gets the row's initial state. One chunk-kernel call over the segments leaves each checkpoint as the final state of its row's first segment. The tails (shorter than one block) started from a zero state there, so a second, small call reruns them from their checkpoints, and their outputs and final states replace the first call's. Both calls reuse the existing per-backend metadata builder.
- **Export**: conv window and recurrent state are stored by #60050's shared `MambaPrefillCheckpointExporter`. Its `recurrent_rows` argument selects each checkpoint directly from the split-state buffer.
- **Opt-in**: the Qwen GDN layer declares checkpoint alignment 1 for Triton/FLA and FlyDSL. #60050's shared all-Mamba-layer check then reserves one checkpoint block only when every Mamba layer can export a checkpoint. The metadata builder turns the split on for Qwen GDN layers, checked by layer type, whose spec reserves a checkpoint block. It does not key off the alignment value: KDA layers sharing the builder also reserve checkpoint blocks, and the spec may carry a shared Mamba checkpoint grid instead, as #61601 proposes. If a checkpoint is scheduled but neither the FlashInfer plan nor the split is set, `_forward_core` fails instead of leaving the reserved block unwritten.
- **Cost**: only steps with a checkpointed prefill pay: per GDN layer, a second chunk-kernel call over the tails, one export kernel and gathers/scatters. Where both arms run the same single step (an 8000-token prompt on a 400-token block), this measured +2 ms (+0.4%) at concurrency 1.
- **Concurrency 1**: TTFT is +11% because the PR runs the 8000-token prompt in one step (578 ms) where the baseline runs 7616 + 384 tokens in two (520–531 ms over two runs). The baseline's own single 8000-token step also takes 579 ms. At concurrency 4 and 16, the baseline's extra tail step delays other requests' prefills, and that dominates.
- **Limitations**: not enabled with speculative decoding or `prefix_match_unit` smaller than the block size. Partial-block prefix hits and speculative block relocation interact with checkpoint blocks in ways not validated here. CUDA and ROCm only.
- **Not a duplicate**: #60050 covers FlashInfer; this PR now builds on its shared checkpoint declaration/export mechanism for Triton/FLA and FlyDSL. #55873 / #55875 / #55876 add application-directed checkpoints.
- **Placement**: backend-neutral split execution lives in `gdn/prefill_checkpoint.py` instead of further growing `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`; backend metadata stays in `gdn_attn.py`.

- this PR: `prefill_checkpoint_alignment=alignment`, which is `GDN_SPLIT_CHECKPOINT_ALIGNMENT` (= 1) on Triton/FLA and FlyDSL;
- #61601: `prefill_checkpoint_alignment=get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_grid(vllm_config)`.

The builder in this PR turns the split on only when `checkpoint_alignment == GDN_SPLIT_CHECKPOINT_ALIGNMENT`. If the conflict is resolved to #61601's grid (16 with `prefix_match_unit` 16, else the block size), the split stays off. But the spec still declares `num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks=1`, so the scheduler can stop splitting at the checkpoint, and the manager can publish a checkpoint block that the forward never writes. Nothing would fail at once; a later prefix hit would read a stale state. I found this by reading the two diffs; I have not reproduced it in a test. Keying `split_prefill_checkpoints` off the backend and `num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks > 0`, instead of the alignment value, would make the two PRs independent of merge order.

**2. Data for spec decoding with `prefix_match_unit` < block.** This PR is off with speculative decoding and with `prefix_match_unit` smaller than the block. Our deployment has both (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 with MTP 3, `--prefix-match-unit 16`, block 480, 8 × A100, multi-turn agentic workload with about 98 % prefix-cache hits), so it keeps every split:
- A scheduler step log shows each prefill admission (median 2 requests, 1,743 new tokens, which fit in one 2,048-token step) running as a chain of 3–5 mixed steps.
- `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split` on a stub scheduler with that configuration (20,000 simulated admissions) gives 3.43 mixed steps per admission today and 2.33 with this PR's scheduler rule. - On our model a mixed step costs much more than a decode step, so each removed step counts.

+"""Internal prefill checkpoints for GDN chunk kernels that only return final
+states (Triton/FLA, AITER FlyDSL).

+Each checkpointed prefill row is cut in two at its checkpoint: the head's final
+state is the checkpoint, and the tail, shorter than one block, is rerun from it.

+

+from dataclasses import dataclass

+ChunkKernelMetadata = tuple[torch.Tensor | None, torch.Tensor | None, object | None]
+
+
+@dataclass
+class GDNPrefillCheckpointSplit:
+    # cu_seqlens of the prefill rows, with each checkpointed row cut in two.
+    seg_bounds: torch.Tensor
+    seg_kernel_metadata: ChunkKernelMetadata
+    # First segment of each prefill row.
+    first_seg: torch.Tensor
+    # Prefill row of each checkpoint.
+    ckpt_rows: torch.Tensor
+    # Prefill-relative token indices of the tails, and their cu_seqlens.
+    tail_tokens: torch.Tensor
+    tail_bounds: torch.Tensor
+    tail_kernel_metadata: ChunkKernelMetadata
+    # Checkpoint of each row of MambaPrefillCheckpointMetadata, 0 if none.
+    rows: torch.Tensor
+

+def build_gdn_prefill_checkpoint_split(
+    query_start_loc: list[int],
+    offsets: list[int],
+    num_decodes: int,
+    device: torch.device,
+    kernel_metadata: Callable[[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], ChunkKernelMetadata],
+) -> GDNPrefillCheckpointSplit | None:
+    """Plan the split on the host, so the forward pass does not sync.
+
+    Args:
+        query_start_loc: cu_seqlens of the non-spec rows.
+        offsets: checkpoint offset into each row's query, 0 for none.
+        num_decodes: number of leading decode rows.
+        device: device of the returned tensors.
+        kernel_metadata: chunk-kernel metadata of (cu_seqlens, cu_seqlens_cpu).
+
+    """
+    assert not any(offsets[:num_decodes])
+    base = query_start_loc[num_decodes]
+    seg_bounds: list[int] = []
+    first_seg: list[int] = []
+    ckpt_rows: list[int] = []
+    tail_tokens: list[int] = []
+    tail_bounds = [0]
+    rows = [0] * len(offsets)
+    for prefill_row, row in enumerate(range(num_decodes, len(offsets))):
+        start = query_start_loc[row] - base
+        end = query_start_loc[row + 1] - base
+        offset = offsets[row]
+        first_seg.append(len(seg_bounds))
+        seg_bounds.append(start)
+        if offset:
+            assert 0 < offset < end - start
+            rows[row] = len(ckpt_rows)
+            ckpt_rows.append(prefill_row)
+            seg_bounds.append(start + offset)
+            tail_tokens.extend(range(start + offset, end))
+            tail_bounds.append(tail_bounds[-1] + end - start - offset)
+    if not ckpt_rows:
+        return None
+    seg_bounds.append(query_start_loc[-1] - base)
+
+    def to_device(data: list[int]) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return async_tensor_h2d(data, device=device, dtype=torch.int64)
+
+    def with_metadata(bounds: list[int]) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ChunkKernelMetadata]:
+        bounds_cpu = torch.tensor(bounds, dtype=torch.int32)
+        bounds_gpu = async_tensor_h2d(bounds_cpu, device=device)
+        return bounds_gpu, kernel_metadata(bounds_gpu, bounds_cpu)
+
+    seg_bounds_gpu, seg_kernel_metadata = with_metadata(seg_bounds)
+    tail_bounds_gpu, tail_kernel_metadata = with_metadata(tail_bounds)
+    return GDNPrefillCheckpointSplit(
+        seg_bounds=seg_bounds_gpu,
+        seg_kernel_metadata=seg_kernel_metadata,
+        first_seg=to_device(first_seg),
+        ckpt_rows=to_device(ckpt_rows),
+        tail_tokens=to_device(tail_tokens),
+        tail_bounds=tail_bounds_gpu,
+        tail_kernel_metadata=tail_kernel_metadata,
+        rows=to_device(rows),
+    )
+
+
+def chunk_gated_delta_rule_with_checkpoints(
+    chunk_gated_delta_rule: Callable[..., tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]],
+    split: GDNPrefillCheckpointSplit,
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    v: torch.Tensor,
+    g: torch.Tensor,
+    beta: torch.Tensor,
+    initial_state: torch.Tensor,
+    use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel: bool,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Run ``chunk_gated_delta_rule`` on the split rows.
+
+    Returns ``(o, final_state, checkpoint_state)``: ``o`` and ``final_state`` as
+    for the unsplit rows, and one checkpoint state per checkpoint.
+    """
+
+    def run(inputs, state, cu_seqlens, kernel_metadata):
+        chunk_indices, chunk_offsets, aiter_prefill_metadata = kernel_metadata
+        q, k, v, g, beta = inputs
+        return chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+            q=q,
+            k=k,
+            v=v,
+            g=g,
+            beta=beta,
+            initial_state=state,
+            output_final_state=True,
+            cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+            chunk_indices=chunk_indices,
+            chunk_offsets=chunk_offsets,
+            use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel,
+            aiter_prefill_metadata=aiter_prefill_metadata,
+        )

+    inputs = (q, k, v, g, beta)
+    num_segs = split.seg_bounds.numel() - 1
+    split_state = initial_state.new_zeros((num_segs, *initial_state.shape[1:]))
+    split_state.index_copy_(0, split.first_seg, initial_state)
+    o, split_final_state = run(
+        inputs, split_state, split.seg_bounds, split.seg_kernel_metadata
+    )
+    # A checkpointed row's first segment ends at its checkpoint.
+    final_state = split_final_state.index_select(0, split.first_seg)
+    checkpoint_state = final_state.index_select(0, split.ckpt_rows)
+
+    # The tails above started from a zero state; rerun them from the checkpoint.
+    tails = split.tail_tokens
+    tail_o, tail_final_state = run(
+        tuple(x.index_select(1, tails) for x in inputs),
+        checkpoint_state.to(initial_state.dtype),
+        split.tail_bounds,
+        split.tail_kernel_metadata,
+    )
+    o.index_copy_(1, tails, tail_o)
+    final_state.index_copy_(0, split.ckpt_rows, tail_final_state)
+    return o, final_state, checkpoint_state

Thanks for this PR. I looked at it while I measured the Mamba `align` split on a hybrid model with MTP. Two notes: a rebase hazard with #61601, and data for the configuration that this PR does not enable yet.

**1. Rebase hazard with #61601 (cc @ZJY0516).** Both PRs change the same line in the Qwen GDN layer's KV spec:
- this PR: `prefill_checkpoint_alignment=alignment`, which is `GDN_SPLIT_CHECKPOINT_ALIGNMENT` (= 1) on Triton/FLA and FlyDSL;
- #61601: `prefill_checkpoint_alignment=get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_grid(vllm_config)`.

The builder in this PR turns the split on only when `checkpoint_alignment == GDN_SPLIT_CHECKPOINT_ALIGNMENT`. If the conflict is resolved to #61601's grid (16 with `prefix_match_unit` 16, else the block size), the split stays off. But the spec still declares `num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks=1`, so the scheduler can stop splitting at the checkpoint, and the manager can publish a checkpoint block that the forward never writes. Nothing would fail at once; a later prefix hit would read a stale state. I found this by reading the two diffs; I have not reproduced it in a test. Keying `split_prefill_checkpoints` off the backend and `num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks > 0`, instead of the alignment value, would make the two PRs independent of merge order.

**2. Data for spec decoding with `prefix_match_unit` < block.** This PR is off with speculative decoding and with `prefix_match_unit` smaller than the block. Our deployment has both (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 with MTP 3, `--prefix-match-unit 16`, block 480, 8 × A100, multi-turn agentic workload with about 98 % prefix-cache hits), so it keeps every split:
- A scheduler step log shows each prefill admission (median 2 requests, 1,743 new tokens, which fit in one 2,048-token step) running as a chain of 3–5 mixed steps.
- `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split` on a stub scheduler with that configuration (20,000 simulated admissions) gives 3.43 mixed steps per admission today and 2.33 with this PR's scheduler rule. With this PR, #60888's column rule and #61601's PLE checkpoints, and with the spec-decode and unit gates removed, it gives 1.01.
- On our model a mixed step costs much more than a decode step, so each removed step counts.

I have a local prototype of the spec-decode and unit-16 enablement on top of this PR, #60888 and #61601 (CPU tests only, not yet run on GPU). I can send it as a follow-up after these land, if that is useful.

Thanks for catching this interaction and for sharing the measurements.

**1. Rebase hazard with #61601.** You're right. On the previous head, if #61601's shared checkpoint grid (not 1) replaced the Qwen GDN alignment, an eligible final prefill could still get internal-checkpoint metadata while `split_prefill_checkpoints` stayed off. The scheduler would then skip the boundary split, and `MambaManager` would later publish the reserved checkpoint block although the forward never exported its state.

Fixed in 49b7f8677:

- Split planning no longer uses the alignment value as a layer-type tag. It requires a Triton/FLA or FlyDSL backend, a reserved checkpoint block, and Qwen GDN layers in the cache group.
- The layer check is needed because backend plus `num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks > 0` alone would also turn the split on for KDA users of the shared builder that reserve checkpoint blocks, notably `KimiK3ROCmKDAMetadataBuilder`, which exports its checkpoints through its own path. With MTP, a batch mixing spec-decode rows and a checkpointed prefill would then hit the split planner's `assert spec_sequence_masks is None`.
- `_forward_core` now fails loudly if a Qwen GDN layer receives checkpoint metadata without a FlashInfer plan or a split plan, instead of leaving the block unwritten.
- The main test now takes the spec from `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention.get_kv_cache_spec` and covers the fail-fast path. A new test checks that the builder enables the split for a Qwen GDN layer with either alignment 1 or the block size, and not for another layer on the GDN backend.

So whichever of the two PRs lands second can take #61601's `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_grid(vllm_config)` line as is. I revalidated the current head on 8x MI308X with the related tests, GSM8K, and prefix-hit continuation checks; details are in the updated description. cc @ZJY0516

MTP with `prefix_match_unit` < block.** Both gates stay in this PR: the split planner does not handle the spec-decode row layout yet, and sub-block checkpoints have not been validated on this path. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next also needs #61601, or equivalent PLE checkpoint support, before the scheduler takes any internal checkpoint, since every Mamba group has to export one.

I haven't reproduced the exact 3.43 / 2.33 / 1.01 figures, but the direction matches how `_mamba_block_aligned_split` places its stops: a valid internal checkpoint removes the block-boundary and tail stops, and #60888's column rule makes it valid for more mid-block starts. A follow-up after these land sounds useful; GPU accuracy runs with real prefix hits (multi-turn GSM8K, for example) would be the main thing needed to enable the spec-decode and unit-16 paths.
